text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The major dams supplying Windhoek with water are expected to run dry by next April if no significant rainfall occurs.
- Stringent new regulations for meat imports to South Africa have resulted in losses for the Namibian meat industry amounting to millions of dollars.
- A new pressure group consisting of civil servants aims to take the Government Institutions Pension Fund (GIPF) to court, claiming that it operates contrary to its own rules.
- Enormous damage is being done to business and the Telecom industry due to the increasing theft of copper telephone cables.
